purpose: Reference evidence for V10 isolated Euler schedule qualification, following the V9 quality No-Go. This file does not report a model run or product Go.

findings: For strength below one, initialization adds scheduler noise to encoded image latents.
At nominal 20 steps and strength 0.99, the effective schedule skips its first entry and has 19 denoising steps.
The nine-channel UNet receives encoded masked image and mask in both classifier-free guidance batches.
Per-step original-latent replacement is restricted to four-channel UNets; this is a separate algorithm difference from the SDK and is not changed by this schedule experiment.
The model-configured leading schedule multiplies reversed step indices by integer train-step/inference-step ratio and adds steps_offset.
At 1000 training steps, 20 nominal inference steps, offset 1: 951,901,...,1; the pipeline strength slice then selects 901,851,...,1.
Sigmas derive from cumulative products of scaled-linear betas; linear interpolation is selected by the model config and a terminal zero is appended.
Euler noise initialization, input scaling and epsilon update agree algebraically with the pinned SDK CompVis/Euler route; this does not establish floating-point or full-pipeline equivalence.

modelScheduler.retrieval: Read exact verified offline source-model input; unchanged pinned original model configuration.

nativeComparison.finding: DiscreteScheduler uses a linspace-like 999-to-0 sequence. CompVis uses original latent plus sigma-scaled noise and standard epsilon Euler algebra. Integer target timesteps avoid the SDK log-sigma interpolation difference at fractional timesteps.

The SDK strength slice starts at sample_steps-floor(sample_steps*strength)-1. For the baseline 20 and 0.99 it starts at zero, retaining 20 steps; for an already selected 19-step custom schedule and 0.99 it also starts at zero, retaining those 19. Denoise-mask dilation remains unchanged.
The public custom-sigma count overrides total/sample step count with count minus one.
The public sample-parameter struct exposes custom_sigmas and custom_sigmas_count.
Blending is active only if the denoise mask contains a value other than one. Disabling it is therefore a no-op when the dilated fixture mask is all one.

numericalComparison.method: Independent Python standard-library double-precision illustration alongside the actual CPU float32 reference-assignment execution recorded below; the illustration is not PyTorch float32 bit identity.

experiment.singleChangedImageFactor: Euler noise schedule, including model-configured leading timestep placement and strength-based initial selection, supplied through the public custom_sigmas API.
experiment.unchanged: Pinned weights/export, seed, prompts, CFG8, nominal20 steps, strength0.99, Euler update, nearest-mask V9 correction, CPU RNG, batching, precision, VAE tiling, native geometry, final mask/compositor and latent blending.
experiment.decisionRule: Run the identical mandatory fixture and current compositor replay; independent visual failure stops this candidate before a full series. Passing one image does not satisfy the complete quality, memory, latency, preview and cooperative-cancellation gates.
claimsExcluded: Full reference implementation or pixel equivalence
Proven cause of V9 black outlines or halos
Quality improvement before actual inference and review
Passing process containment as a cooperative cancellation or product Go

numericReferenceExecution.selection: Pipeline get_timesteps: t_start = 20 - min(int(20 * 0.99),20) = 1. Select corresponding sigma tail including terminal zero.
numericReferenceExecution.reproduction: Parse the byte-verified official Euler source with ast.parse. For each executedAssignmentStartLines entry, select the unique ast.Assign or ast.AugAssign beginning on that line and compile as an ast.Module. Execute in one shared environment containing torch, numpy as np, self.config from the pinned model scheduler config (plus final_sigmas_type zero), self.num_inference_steps and num_inference_steps 20, beta_start 0.00085, beta_end 0.012, num_train_timesteps 1000, and device cpu. Select sigmas[1:] and timesteps[1:] as determined by the independently verified pipeline strength rule. Compare canonical little-endian float32 bytes.
